To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Hamilton-Diract formulation of GR is canonical, it preserves diffeomorphism symmetry in 4D space-time, it gives rise to a 4D diffeomorphism algebra and that the Dirac and ADM Hamiltonians are related by a canonical transformation.

(i) Dirac’s Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein’s theory does not require a 3 +1 decomposition of spacetimes; (ii) Dirac’s theory is diffeomorphism covariant and this is not an artifact of a 3 +4 decomposition of spacetimes.

the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein’s theory of gravitation is a four-dimensional diffeomorphic-invariant canonical theory of gravity, which is equivalent to Einstein’s field equations, and that the Dirac Hamiltonization of GR is not equivalent to the ADM Hamiltonization of GR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein’s theory of general relativity.
the canonical treatment of general relativity.
clarifying some misconceptions and misunderstandings that have arisen about the canonical treatment of GR and its relation to the ADM formulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein’s theory of GR is a canonical formulation, and that the canonical formulation of GR has the full diffeomorphism symmetry of four-dimensional spacetime.
the Hamiltonian formulation of the Dirac approach to GR is equivalent to the ADM formulation and that the Dirac Hamilton-DeWitt approach to GR is also equivalent to the ADM one.

the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein’s equations is a canonical formulation of the equations of motion of the metric field gμν, which is equivalent to the standard formulation, and that the Hamiltonian approach does not break diffeomorphism symmetry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(i–ii) the canonical approach does not require a 3 +1 decomposition of spacetimes and the Hamiltonian formulation does not break the symmetry between space-like and time-like hypersurfaces; (iii) the Dirac and ADM formulations are equivalent; (iv) there is no field-dependent or non-covariant diffeomorphism constraint; (v) the canonical approach is a valid and useful tool for studying GR.

the Hamiltonian formalism of GR, which is based on a Hamiltonian analysis of the Einstein-Hilbert action, can be developed without the use of a foliation of spacetime and without the use of lapse and shift functions.
the Dirac Hamilton-Dirac Hamiltonian formulation for General Relativity is not equivalent to the ADM formulation, but the two approaches are related by a non-canonical transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the canonical treatment of GR does not require any 3+1 decomposition of spacetimes.
one can use the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein’s equations without breaking the diffeomorphism symmetry in four-dimensional spacetime.
one should not confuse a 3 +1 decomposition of spacetimes with the canonical treatment of GR.
